caption:
Z.ai released GLM-5.4, a coding model that runs some of its layers twice instead of adding new ones.

What happened: On 23 Nov, Z.ai (@Zai_org) announced GLM-5.4, its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer. Its docs say it reuses 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model across two passes, which gives a deeper network without adding parameters. It is live for GLM Coding Plan users now, and the public API comes after a security assessment.

Why it matters for you: In a normal Transformer each layer runs once. Here the same weights refine their own output a second time. It is the trade you make when you call one function in a loop instead of copy-pasting it: less to store, more compute per run.

Takeaway: Z.ai names the cost too. The model can get caught in overly long "marathon thinking" loops. Every design has a price, and naming it is what interviewers listen for.

Would you pick a model that thinks longer but is cheaper to host?

Source: https://x.com/Zai_org/status/2124811995912286352 and https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.4
